The infinite graph

A graph can hold stored facts, derive facts through a virtual provider, or combine both. Callers read a specified scope at a pinned revision.

Contract illustration
Master graphRule / ontology
◉ Active+ Added− RemovedΔ Changed× Rejected
The rule
What the contract requires
Reads pin a revision, scope and work budget, and report whether the answer is complete.
The boundary
Scope and constraints
Infinite extents require finite query scopes. Symbolic patches for virtual-definition changes remain an open design decision.
Example · C#
Read a finite neighborhood
Full source ↗
Pin a graph revision, scope and work budget for stored or virtual data.
UsageExamples.cs
public static ReadGraph Neighborhood(GraphVersion version, EntityId root) =>
    new(new RequestId("neighborhood"), version,
        new GraphScope([root], 2, [new TypeId("Calls")]),
        new WorkBudget(MaximumFacts: 10_000, MaximumSteps: 100_000),
        Continuation: null);
// Submit through IGraphSpace.ReadAsync for stored or virtual graphs.
// Inspect Complete, MoreAvailable, BudgetExhausted and Unavailable on each
// returned page. A page by itself does not imply a complete neighborhood.
Compile-checked caller example. Execution requires implementations of the injected interfaces.
